text:
maya_marketing: hey runtime — were finalizing the webinar narrative and need a short run to validate numbers and an A/B for the launch blog. can you help with cost/throughput numbers + an AB comparison of quant profiles?
dave_marketing: specifically we want: per-token cost estimate (hosted pricing) extrapolated from Dedicated run, p50/p95 latencies, tokens/sec, and % SLO breaches (>200ms) for interactive. one-slide summary for the blog + a small appendix CSV.
hana_runtime: can do. need precise model names, target quant profiles, and whether the blog AB should compare quality or just perf/cost. also do you want warmup/warm cache runs or cold only?
maya_marketing: good Qs. scope: 1) models: redwood-base-fp16 and redwood-base-4bit (use q4_1) 2) AB: perf+cost only (we'll run separate evals for quality) 3) sequences: 32 (short chat), 256 (typical), 512 (longish) 4) shapes: interactive (concurrency=6, streaming enabled), burst (concurrency=128, batching), baseline single-stream 5) KV cache: enabled for interactive runs 6) outputs: one aggregated CSV per model+quant with columns we can paste into blog table, and a README with commits/docker tags.
pranav_runtime: adding: include estimated hosted-per-token cost column (marketing wants a back-of-envelope using hosted price-per-1M tokens). we'll compute hosted cost from Dedicated run using token/sec and cost-rate table — we'll include the formula in README.
dave_marketing: also include a tiny line for the blog: "typical latency (p95) on interactive is X ms; throughput for bulk is Y tokens/sec" so we can craft copy.
hana_runtime: run plan below (will attach to S3):
```
# run harness snippet
model_variants: ["redwood-base-fp16", "redwood-base-4bit-q4_1"]
seq_lengths: [32,256,512]
concurrency_shapes: {"single":1, "interactive":6, "burst":128}
streaming: [true, false] # stream only for interactive
kv_cache: [on] # on for interactive, off for others
replicates: 4
warmup_requests: 100
max_new_tokens: [32,128,128]
quant_profiles: ["fp16","q4_1"]
export_prefix: "s3://redwood-perf/marketing/webinar_ab/1879998888/"
```
hana_runtime: deliverables: aggregated CSVs with columns: run_id, model_variant, quant, seq_len, concurrency, stream, p50_ms, p95_ms, p99_ms, tokens_per_sec, slo_200ms_pct, avg_batch_size, avg_batch_wait_ms, kv_hit_rate, gpu_mem_mb, gpu_util_pct, commit, docker_tag, hosted_cost_per_1M_tokens_est_usd.
pranav_runtime: estimation note: well annotate how hosted cost was extrapolated (dedicated hourly cost / tokens/sec -> cost/token). marketing: confirm the hosted price-per-1M you want used or should we use current public list price?
maya_marketing: use current public hosted price; include both raw estimate and the formula so we can show transparency. and please attach the short curl snippet for smoke check we can run during the webinar demo.
hana_runtime: curl sample we'll place in README:```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \\
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \\
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\
  -d '{"model":"redwood-base-fp16","input":"Hello","max_new_tokens":32,"stream":false}'
```
dave_marketing: timeline: need the slide-ready numbers in 48 hours. can you surface early draft CSV by tomorrow noon so we can start writing?
hana_runtime: pushing to schedule. rough estimate: ~8 hours of runs for both variants across shapes (on Dedicated). will try to finish overnight and post draft CSV to S3 by 2026-03-26 12:00 UTC.
perf-bot: upload complete -> s3://redwood-perf/marketing/webinar_ab/1879998888/draft/manifest.json
pranav_runtime: if we hit high variance (>20% p95 across replicates) we'll rerun those shapes and annotate instability in the README. also flagging memory pressure for q4_1 on the 512 seq; may need to drop batch size.
maya_marketing: good call. please ping @dave_marketing and @maya_marketing if any shape is flaky so we can decide to drop it for the blog. thanks all 680
dave_marketing: thanks team. after you post the draft CSV we'll pair on a quick table copy for the blog and the single slide.
hana_runtime: will post links and the commit/digest in the README with run IDs when done. starting runs now.
